concerns: The code, data manifests, and model weights are described as forthcoming in a 'versioned software release' rather than currently available, making independent reproducibility unverifiable at submission time; the paper's own resource availability section confirms this (B0057).

The paper references several future-dated or preprint-only works as key baselines and components (e.g., STACK ref 15 dated 2026, Rhaister ref 40 dated 2026, PULSAR ref 41 dated 2025, Parse PBMC atlas ref 39 dated 2025), none of which are independently published at the time of this preprint, creating circular or unverifiable dependency chains for the evaluation.

The primary forecasting result on the common-gene-space benchmark ties the Immune World Model with the condition-mean baseline (both 0.46 Δcos; B0033), which is a simple non-parametric aggregator, substantially weakening the central action-conditioned dynamics claim; the paper acknowledges this but the discussion does not fully resolve whether per-action gains compensate for this aggregate tie.

The anti-PD-1 patient-state AUC of 0.92 (LOO-CV, n unspecified but implied small given 95% CI 0.79–1.00; B0034/B0035) is based on leave-one-out cross-validation on what appears to be a small cohort, and the wide confidence intervals indicate high uncertainty; the sample size is not explicitly stated in the accessible text, limiting interpretability of this headline result.

The 'governed evolutionary AI Scientist' (Agent Genesis) is a central methodological claim, but the builder benchmark compares the EvoIWM-building Scientist against named commercial LLM versions (DeepSeek V4, Claude S5, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.6, Qwen 3.6) that do not correspond to any publicly released model versions as of the manuscript's stated arXiv date (September 2026), making the comparison unverifiable and raising concerns about the manuscript's internal consistency.

The therapeutic hypothesis (IL-36γ plus SIRPα inhibition) is explicitly unvalidated experimentally (B0055), which is acceptable for a computational study, but the nomination rests partly on zero-shot inference from OrthJEPA and SE-PCA, which are described as internal configuration labels rather than independently validated methods (B0091/B0092), limiting the strength of the biological evidence chain.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The contribution is substantive and scoped, the method is adequately described, evaluation is meaningful across multiple scales with appropriate controls and uncertainty reporting, and claims are appropriately qualified with limitations compatible with the computational scope.

The Immune World Model–building Scientist constructed the model while addressing a dis-
tinct problem: how to develop such a model while preserving a testable record of the choices that
produced it. Agent Genesis treated architecture changes, repairs, and evaluation procedures as
versioned proposals evaluated under common budgets and prespecified gates. Consequently,

blocking_reasons: The code, data manifests, and model weights are described as forthcoming in a 'versioned software release' rather than currently available, making independent reproducibility unverifiable at submission time; the paper's own resource availability section confirms this (B0057).

The paper references several future-dated or preprint-only works as key baselines and components (e.g., STACK ref 15 dated 2026, Rhaister ref 40 dated 2026, PULSAR ref 41 dated 2025, Parse PBMC atlas ref 39 dated 2025), none of which are independently published at the time of this preprint, creating circular or unverifiable dependency chains for the evaluation.

The primary forecasting result on the common-gene-space benchmark ties the Immune World Model with the condition-mean baseline (both 0.46 Δcos; B0033), which is a simple non-parametric aggregator, substantially weakening the central action-conditioned dynamics claim; the paper acknowledges this but the discussion does not fully resolve whether per-action gains compensate for this aggregate tie.

The anti-PD-1 patient-state AUC of 0.92 (LOO-CV, n unspecified but implied small given 95% CI 0.79–1.00; B0034/B0035) is based on leave-one-out cross-validation on what appears to be a small cohort, and the wide confidence intervals indicate high uncertainty; the sample size is not explicitly stated in the accessible text, limiting interpretability of this headline result.

The 'governed evolutionary AI Scientist' (Agent Genesis) is a central methodological claim, but the builder benchmark compares the EvoIWM-building Scientist against named commercial LLM versions (DeepSeek V4, Claude S5, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.6, Qwen 3.6) that do not correspond to any publicly released model versions as of the manuscript's stated arXiv date (September 2026), making the comparison unverifiable and raising concerns about the manuscript's internal consistency.

The therapeutic hypothesis (IL-36γ plus SIRPα inhibition) is explicitly unvalidated experimentally (B0055), which is acceptable for a computational study, but the nomination rests partly on zero-shot inference from OrthJEPA and SE-PCA, which are described as internal configuration labels rather than independently validated methods (B0091/B0092), limiting the strength of the biological evidence chain.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of multiscale forecasting and hypothesis nomination are supported by the reported benchmarks and ablations, and the therapeutic hypothesis is explicitly framed as model-derived and prospectively testable rather than validated.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation includes locked external-capability probes, few-shot cellular forecasting, tissue and individual-context benchmarks, action composition, and a governed self-correction audit, with confidence intervals and negative results reported where relevant.
primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that experimental confirmation, formal pharmacological synergy, cohort-level validation of recursive rollout, and larger external clinical cohorts remain to be established.
primary.method_assessment: The structured encoder, action-conditioned transition, and structured decoder are described with formal equations and module-level ablations; the AI Scientist development process is documented with versioned lineage, predeclared promotion gates, and locked confirmation manifests.
primary.quality_rationale: The contribution is substantive and scoped, the method is adequately described, evaluation is meaningful across multiple scales with appropriate controls and uncertainty reporting, and claims are appropriately qualified with limitations compatible with the computational scope.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents the Immune World Model, an action-conditioned multiscale model that learns intervention-dependent transitions across cellular, tissue, and individual immune states, constructed via a governed evolutionary AI Scientist and frozen before independent confirmation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are generally well supported by the reported results: reviewer-guided revision improves more than fixed-prompt self-revision, Stanford Reviewer independently confirms upward trajectories, and the execution-versus-idea resolution asymmetry is quantified and discussed. The abstract's headline numbers match the body, and the authors appropriately frame the finding that novelty concerns are rarely resolved.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is meaningful and multi-layered: reviewer quality is separately benchmarked against baselines on 650 ICLR papers with pairwise judging and human-alignment checks, and revision outcomes are measured on 30 papers across five domains with score trajectories, an external Stanford Reviewer evaluation of human-initialized revisions, and a weakness-resolution analysis (128/150 execution vs 2/18 idea weaknesses). Controls include autonomous self-revision with a fixed prompt and AI-initialized guidance, isolating the effect of iterative reviewer feedback.
primary.limitations: The evaluation set is small (30 papers) and constrained to ICLR papers reproducible on a single 96 GB GPU, with cost (~$65/paper) cited as the limiting factor. The same reviewer both guides and scores the reviewer-driven conditions, though the external Stanford Reviewer evaluation partially mitigates this circularity; Stanford Reviewer is not applied to the AI-initialized or self-revision conditions.
primary.method_assessment: The system design is described in adequate detail: the scientist retains full revision history and addresses each reviewer concern through code edits, literature search, experiment execution, and manuscript updates, while the reviewer independently evaluates only the current manuscript with no memory of prior drafts or scores. The reviewer uses a structured multi-phase process with deep literature search over an indexed arXiv corpus, temporal grounding, and a verification pass.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper makes a substantive, clearly scoped contribution with a well-described system, appropriate controls, independent external evaluation, and a nuanced characterization of what iterative revision can and cannot improve. The main weaknesses are acknowledged and bounded by the study design, and the evidence supports the stated claims without overclaiming.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces AppliedScientist, a closed-loop system that iteratively revises rejected papers' implementation, experiments, and manuscript under fresh independent AI reviews, while keeping the central research contribution fixed. It contributes a benchmark of reviewer-guided versus fixed-prompt self-revision across 30 ICLR papers and a characterization of which reviewer weaknesses revision can resolve.
